hints: Focus on counting every carbon and hydrogen carefully, remembering that each corner in a skeletal formula is a carbon with enough hydrogens to make four bonds.
Start with option A, a five-membered ring with a C=O and one methyl branch, and work out its total C count and H count.
Now count the others the same way and look for which one gives exactly 6 carbons and 10 hydrogens, remembering a ring or a double bond each removes two hydrogens.
walkthrough:
**Recall how to count from skeletal structures**

Great, let us take this calmly together. Every line end or corner is a carbon, and each carbon needs four bonds in total.

Rule to use:
$$\text{missing bonds on C = bonds to H}$$

**Count option A**

Option A is 3-methylcyclopentanone. The ring has 5 carbons plus 1 carbon in the methyl group, so 6 carbons in total.

For hydrogens: $\text{C=O}$ carbon has 0 H, two $\text{CH}_2$ groups have $2+2$ H, one CH has 1 H, one $\text{CH(CH}_3)$ has $1+3$ H. That is $2+2+1+1+3 = 9$? Wait, check again carefully: ring gives 7 H plus methyl gives 3 H, total 10 H. So $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

**Check the others and conclude**

Option B is $\text{CH}_3\text{COC(CH}_3)_3$, which has 6 carbons but $3+9 = 12$ hydrogens, so $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$.

Option C is cyclohex-2-en-1-one, 6 carbons with one ring plus one C=C plus one C=O, so it loses extra hydrogens to give $\text{C}_6\text{H}_8\text{O}$. Option D is an unsaturated alcohol with one C=C only, giving $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$. Only A matches.

options.A: Correct. 5 ring carbons + 1 methyl carbon = 6 carbons. Cyclopentanone alone is C5H8O, replacing one H by CH3 adds CH2, giving C6H10O. Hydrogen count fits perfectly.
options.B: Incorrect. This is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one, CH3COC(CH3)3. It is saturated and acyclic, so with 6 carbons it must be C6H12O. Students who forget to add all nine hydrogens on the tert-butyl group often undercount H.
options.C: Incorrect. This is cyclohexenone. It has a ring (minus 2 H) plus a C=C (minus 2 H) plus a C=O, giving C6H8O, two hydrogens too few. The trap is to count only the ring and forget the extra unsaturation from the double bond.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 2,3-dimethylbut-3-en-1-ol. It has 6 carbons and only one C=C, so it is C6H12O. The trap is to miscount the branched skeleton or to think the OH removes hydrogens, but an alcohol O does not change the H count relative to alkene here.
